issue_context.title: (4.4.beta3) GPUParticles3D spawn angle does not work when particle one_shot is true.
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.4.beta3.
-  Not reproducible in 4.3.stable

### System information

Godot v4.4.beta3 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6636) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-9900KF CPU @ 3.60GHz (16 threads)

### Issue description

When one_shot is true in a GPUParticles3D node, spawn angle has no effect. If one_shot is false, spawn angle works correctly. 

### Steps to reproduce

-Add GPUParrticles3D node
-Add new particle process material
- Spawn -> angle -> min 0 to max 360
- (optional: set acceleration -> gravity to zero for clarity)
- Add quadmesh as draw pass 1 
- Add new standard material 3d to material slot in draw pass 1 quadmesh
- In material, Albedo -> texture -> icon.svg
- In material, Billboard -> mode -> Particle Billboard (also does not work with particle flags rotate y and disable z per documentation)
- Back at top, set lifetime to .05 and amount to 1
- test emitting with both one_shot enabled and disabled and you will see that no random rotation is applied if one_shot = true 
- (not reproducible in 4.3.stable)


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[one_shot_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18809321/one_shot_mrp.zip)
comments:
I can reproduce the issue with the MRP in latest `master` (f42e612da286b14b3a50eff7935615b3bc132c37). It seems to be a regression introduced between 4.4.dev7 and 4.4.beta1.
I suspect #92089 (didn't test to confirm). CC @QbieShay
@akien-mga I was ready to say that i reverted pr #92089 and seems be the culprit 😆

So. I went to look at the mrp. This is what's happening now in the particles

1. On instantiation, particles are given a random seed.
2. If they use fixed seed, the fixed seed is subsequently set.

When not using oneshot, the seed is also not randomized, but every subsequent cycle of the particles creates a new seed. This is visible with oneshot because there's only one cycle for the emission, but it's a problem for both cases.

The only way currently to get the seed to re-randomize is to call restart().

I need to discuss with rendering folks what's the proper solution. I have a PR ready that re-randomizes at every emission and therefore preserves previous behaviour, but i feel like i'll be shooting myself in the foot with it for future tooling and improvements ..
